correctness.rationale: A positive-coordinate support of a fixed point is an invariant matching. Each edge orbit projects surjectively onto both transitive shores; the matching condition forces orbit size equal to both shore sizes. Hence admissible orbits are graphs of equivariant perfect matchings and cannot coexist. The unique invariant point in each orbit simplex is its barycenter. All edge cases and integral H0 follow. Reproducible independent checks exhaust 226 small invariant graphs and centralizers through degree six.

value.rationale: A natural and broad fixed-point classification for matching complexes of all finite bipartite graphs with shore-transitive side-preserving group actions, converting an equivariant topological invariant into exact counts of equivariant bijections and permutation centralizers. In the complete square case it gives an exact classification for every transitive subgroup, sharp 1..n component range, and integral homology; this is not a one-off parameter choice or a negative normalisation check.
